scope: Retrospective structured descriptions of selected relationships in nine retained sessions; one analyst, no independent reliability estimate and no prevalence coding.

cases.title: One local test, two evidential roles
cases.expectation: Revision 3, before batches 11-12, predicts a substantial response if the alternative component is the active coordinate.
cases.execution: Batch 11 tests the component alone; batch 12 adds a large component spike to a small reagent charge. Both committed tests remain near the observed response plateau.
cases.revision: Revision 4 withdraws support for the tested mapping while retaining buffering, saturation and unidentified-coordinate explanations.
cases.supported_scope: The executed perturbations oppose the specified mapping prediction. They do not determine the low-loading limit or distinguish a persistent plateau from a dilute transition.
cases.later_use: The extreme-dilution forecast explicitly invokes the component-only result: dissociation 0.092, interval 0.043-0.155, versus reference mean 0.51730. Retrospective review recognizes unresolved low-loading alternatives without receiving truth.
cases.coverage: One fully connected focal trajectory; the 45-session equilibrium distribution contextualizes the outcome but does not establish the frequency of this process.

quotes.quote: A null component response would instead favor an internally buffered/invariant world.
component-as-active-loading hypothesis rejected in tested form
shrink strongly toward the experimentally observed near-invariant baseline because a component-only batch also retained similar responses.

cases.title: A prospective seed-rescue expectation is withdrawn
cases.expectation: Revision 3 proposes repeating the concentrated 0.02 L recipe with 0.05 g seed to test whether particle quality can be rescued.
cases.execution: Batches 10 and 12 share the principal preparation and cooling operations; committed seed changes from 0.02 to 0.05 g. Both assays report fines fraction 1.0.
cases.revision: Revision 4 explicitly disconfirms this prospective rescue expectation and retains a different recipe as the recommendation.
cases.supported_scope: The larger of the two executed doses does not rescue the tested condition. No conclusion about all larger doses or every seeding mechanism follows.
cases.later_use: The recommendation uses an alternative recipe whose noiseless fines fraction is 0.24744 and which satisfies the recorded feasibility criteria. Recovery rankings remain subject to the disclosed definition mismatch.
cases.coverage: One prospective dose contrast and recorded revision; no independent repeat of this exact hypothesis test is claimed.

quotes.quote: Repeat the 0.02 L high-loading recipe using 0.05 g seed.
disconfirming the final prospective rescue hypothesis.

cases.title: A working recipe region guides a new test
cases.expectation: After a feasible 35 ml recipe, revision 4 proposes 32.5 ml as the next boundary test.
cases.execution: Batches 10-12 use 35, 32.5 and 35 ml, with otherwise matching principal operations. Measured fines fractions are 0.14526, 0.03411 and 0.13587.
cases.revision: The final note retains a bounded feasible region and selects the repeated 35 ml recipe. It does not claim that small differences among close recovery values are resolved.
cases.supported_scope: The sequence supports feasibility of the tested recipes. Earlier low-volume failures also changed seed or thermal history, so a sharp concentration threshold is not isolated.
cases.later_use: The proposed intermediate-volume test is executed and the final recommendation passes an independent retest, with fines fraction 0.13392. There is no clean causal estimate of a universal volume effect.
cases.coverage: One prospective test, one same-recipe repeat and one recommendation retest in a single session; these are not independent researcher samples.

quotes.quote: Next test at 0.0325 L targets the boundary.
Its 0.035 L recipe was independently repeated in batch 12 and remained compliant

cases.title: Recognized high purity and altered transfer, first session
cases.expectation: A specific pre-test numerical commitment to invariant purity is not established by this focal comparison; the relevant supported judgment appears in the sealed source account.
cases.execution: Twelve source assays have mean purity 99.09%; the selected recipe passes the recorded retest criteria.
cases.revision: The source account explicitly recognizes impurity rejection and high crystal purity. This is a documented local characterization, not a quantified pre/post learning gain.
cases.supported_scope: High purity is observed in the tested recipes. Transfer still requires judging effects of changed conditions; no universal purity law is inferred.
cases.later_use: Forecast adjustments for solvent, occlusion, concentration and thermal history yield mean purity 86.92%, versus reference 98.45%. Purity MAE is 0.11529 and 0/12 purity intervals cover the reference.
cases.coverage: One of all three sessions in the same world/information cell; all three are retained below.

cases.title: Recognized high purity and altered transfer, second session
cases.expectation: A specific pre-test commitment to unchanged purity is not established by this comparison; the source account explicitly characterizes the observed response.
cases.execution: Twelve source assays have mean purity 98.18%; the recommendation passes the recorded retest criteria.
cases.revision: The report recognizes high purity and a repeatedly feasible process region. It also contains a separate inaccurate seed-dose account; recognizing purity does not validate every other claim in that report.
cases.supported_scope: High purity and recipe feasibility are supported locally. The reported large-dose seed comparison requires separate execution checking.
cases.later_use: Mean purity forecast is 86.33%, versus common reference 98.45%. No claim of forgetting or a shared psychological mechanism is made.
cases.coverage: Second of the three same-cell sessions, rather than a second independently sampled world.

quotes.quote: S2 did give high purity and substantial recovery

cases.title: Recognized high purity and altered transfer, third session
cases.expectation: No specific pre-test invariance commitment is assigned; the comparison concerns established source observations and their subsequent use.
cases.execution: Twelve source assays have mean purity 99.09%; the recommendation passes the recorded retest criteria.
cases.revision: The source account recognizes that observed S2 purities are generally 0.98-1.00 and acknowledges confounding in solvent comparisons.
cases.supported_scope: The observed high-purity region is supported; an independent solvent effect is not identified.
cases.later_use: Mean purity forecast is 89.92%, versus reference 98.45%. This repeats the recognition/forecast contrast, not necessarily the route that produced it.
cases.coverage: Third of all three same-cell sessions; no population probability is estimated from three repeats.

quotes.quote: Low impurity occlusion is consistent with the observed final purities, generally 0.98–1.00 in S2 batches.

cases.title: An intended large-dose test becomes negative evidence
cases.expectation: Revision 4 proposes approximately 2 g cumulative seed, treating 0.05 g as a per-operation allowance.
cases.execution: Batch 10 requests forty additions of 0.05 g; one commits and thirty-nine are rejected. Total committed seed is 0.05 g.
cases.revision: Revision 5 states that increasing seed to about 2 g did not reduce fines and excludes seed mass as the limiting control. Later notes and sealed accounts retain the claim.
cases.supported_scope: The trajectory provides no physical test of 2 g. A failed request is not negative evidence for the scientific dose hypothesis.
cases.later_use: The claimed exclusion persists in the final account and retrospective review. Its independent influence on subsequent actions has not been tested.
cases.coverage: One connected execution/report discrepancy, with a rejection-recognizing counterexample in case 8. Rejection counts across the cohort are not error-prevalence estimates.

quotes.quote: Seed mass is not the limiting control in this range.

cases.title: Rejected additions are correctly recognized
cases.expectation: The attempted repeated addition is checked against its actual execution status; a separate prospective high-dose scientific expectation is not assigned by this focal analysis.
cases.execution: Additional seed requests in batch 2 are rejected by payload bounds.
cases.revision: Revision 2 explicitly records the failed additions and states that one legal seed operation should be used per batch unless the range changes.
cases.supported_scope: The operational conclusion concerns permitted dosing, not a physical effect of the rejected larger dose.
cases.later_use: The recorded decision limits further dosing rather than claiming a successful large-dose test. A causal effect of the note itself is not estimated.
cases.coverage: A selected counterexample showing that rejection need not become a false experimental claim.

quotes.quote: use one legal seed operation per batch unless the current legal range changes.

cases.title: Accurate extrapolation with an unresolved mechanism
cases.expectation: The source account retains multiple explanations for an observed plateau; a directly executed extreme-dilution discriminator is absent from the source action record.
cases.execution: Twelve source batches characterize a plateau without positive-loading assays at or below 1 mM.
cases.revision: An effective soluble-concentration ceiling becomes more specific during forecasting, although it had remained one candidate in the source account.
cases.supported_scope: The source observations do not uniquely identify the ceiling mechanism. Correct extrapolation can use theoretical structure without direct sampling.
cases.later_use: The dilute forecast is relatively accurate; retrospective review still recognizes that its intervals underrepresent the competing persistent-plateau explanation.
cases.coverage: One positive extrapolation counterexample within the first process block; accuracy does not retrospectively make the mechanism experimentally identified.
